claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can accurately capture the size-dependent thermal stability of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Explicit modeling of atomic interactions and surface effects enables MD to capture size-dependent thermal stability.
The initial FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles are synthesized in powder form.
The initial FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have a well-defined microstructure.
Nanoparticle size governs the surface-to-volume ratio.
Changing nanoparticle size alters atomic coordination numbers.
Decreasing nanoparticle size increases the relative influence of surface atoms.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have greater surface disorder.
Greater surface disorder at smaller sizes lowers the effective melting point.
MD simulations can identify the size-dependent thermal response through the early onset of atomic diffusion and structural disordering.
Under identical heating conditions, smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will exhibit lower thermal stability than larger nanoparticles.
Lower thermal stability in smaller nanoparticles will appear as earlier melting or phase transformation.
Bulk FeCuCrCoNi simulated under similar conditions will have higher thermal stability than the nanoparticles.
Bulk FeCuCrCoNi will exhibit more uniform thermal stability and less pronounced size-dependent effects.
The accuracy of the MD results is limited by the fidelity of the interatomic potential used for FeCuCrCoNi.
Classical MD may not fully capture quantum effects in very small nanoparticles.
The appropriateness of existing interatomic potentials for HEAs is uncertain under extreme thermal conditions and at very small sizes.
